2: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “A Dove on Distant Oaks.” A Miktam of David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath. Be merciful to me, O God, for men are hounding me; all day they press their attack.
3: My enemies pursue me all day long, for many proudly assail me.
4: When I am afraid, I put my trust in You.
5: In God, whose word I praise— in God I trust. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
6: All day long they twist my words; all their thoughts are on my demise.
7: They conspire, they lurk, they watch my steps while they wait to take my life.
8: In spite of such sin, will they escape? In Your anger, O God, cast down the nations.
9: You have taken account of my wanderings. Put my tears in Your bottle— are they not in Your book?
10: Then my enemies will retreat on the day I cry for help. By this I will know that God is on my side.
11: In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD, whose word I praise,
12: in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
13: Your vows are upon me, O God; I will render thank offerings to You.
14: For You have delivered my soul from death, and my feet from stumbling, that I may walk before God in the light of life.
